title: not
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how not flips True to False and False to True.
learn: Use not in an if condition
idea: not reverses a boolean, so not True is False and not False is True. It is useful when you care about the opposite of a flag. For example if not game_over: basically means keep going while the game is not over. Put not in front of a condition or a bool variable.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change game_over = False to game_over = True and press Run. You should see Thanks for playing.

practice.text: Set paused = False. If not paused, print Running.
practice.hint: paused is False, so not paused is True. Write if not paused: and put your message in that block.
practice.starterTip: Try if not paused: on one line, then indented underneath: print("Running").
practice.gradingNote: Pass if if not paused prints Running.

practice.text: Print not (3 == 3) and explain in a comment that it is False.
practice.hint: 3 == 3 is True and not flips it to False. Your comment can say that, then print the expression.
practice.starterTip: Keep or add a comment like the starter, then try print(not (3 == 3)). The output should be False.
practice.starter:
# 3 == 3 is True, so not flips it
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if output is False using not.

quiz.question: What is not False?
quiz.correct: Right, not flips False into True.

quiz.question: What does if not ready: mean?
quiz.correct: Yes, you enter the block when ready is False.
quiz.wrong: not ready is only True when ready is False.

quiz.question: What is not (2 < 1)?
quiz.correct: Right, 2 < 1 is False and not False is True.
quiz.wrong: Flip the False comparison to True.
